extracted.intended_audience: aspiring sketch-comedy writers / students or performers learning sketch structure
extracted.subtask_description: Explains a practical, five-point structural method for creating and rewriting short comedy sketches (exposition, introduce joke, heighten, punch, button). Aimed at producing tight, performable sketch scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-Point Structure (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: ALL sketches can fit into the same, simple 5-point structure: Exposition, Introduce the Joke, Heighten the Joke, Punch the Joke, Button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structure is presented as the 'ultimate key' to writing, rewriting, and watching sketches; use it as the backbone for sketch creation. Plug ideas into these beats to reliably produce a sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer the audience's basic questions (WHO, WHY, WHAT) as quickly as possible so they understand the reality of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep this part to about 5 lines of dialogue or less; in script format aim for less than a page (about half a page). Specify who's onstage/camera and their relationships, why they are here now, and what they are doing. Example: quick character introductions and premise (MACY/PAULA ice cream on Mars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce the Joke (the Game)
rubrics_metrics.description: After setting the world, introduce the single crazy/wacky/funny thing (the 'game') that the sketch will explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on ONLY ONE joke/game. The introduce-beat's job is to get that joke started — you don't need to fully explore it yet, just establish the rule or absurdity that will be heightened. Example: 'JENN is throwing a party, but she only has Joni Mitchell CDs.' Warning: tossing multiple competing rules will make the sketch confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heighten the Joke
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the meat of the sketch where you escalate the joke — make it more ridiculous, specific, and extreme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About 95% of your sketch length should come from heightening. Typically heightening happens over three beats, each crazier/funnier than the last. Heightening defines the sketch's tone; different methods of escalation yield very different feels. Example beats: incremental refusals or increasingly absurd interpretations (MAURIE hates games → hates games a lot → really hates games).

rubrics_metrics.name: Break (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cheeky optional moment where the rules are broken for the sake of a laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every sketch needs a break, but when used it can be a small, unexpected aside that plays against established rules (example: MAURIE claims to love Capture the Flag for political reasons). Treat it as a spice — optional and brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch the Joke (exit the game)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a way to end the joke and get out of the central game so the sketch can come to a close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common exit strategies: heighten too far (extreme escalation), introduce the voice of reason who calls out the joke, have a new person enter changing the dynamic, or use a ticking clock/timeout (a timer, movie starting, etc.). Choose an exit that feels logical to the established game and allows closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Button
rubrics_metrics.description: Finish with one last joke — the 'button' — designed to leave the audience laughing as the sketch ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The button should be a final payoff; it can be random or even discredit the sketch's joke. Don't skip it — a strong button slaps a laugh on the end (example: a voice-of-reason character suddenly says something absurd about eating slugs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Joke Focus and Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the sketch centered on a single comedic premise/game and avoid introducing multiple competing jokey rules too early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle appears throughout the structure: clarity early (in exposition), a single game introduced, and escalating that single game. Anti-pattern: tossing out all rules before perfecting them leads to confusion and diminished laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended length proportions for beats: quick exposition (~5 lines or < half page), introduce the joke briefly, and the bulk (~95%) of sketch length devoted to heightening over multiple beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the numeric targets as practical constraints while drafting: they help keep sketches tight and focused. Treat the three-heighten-beat structure as a guide to pacing.
